finding: The new Ship steps 1 and 2 are skipped by the refusal rows that lead to a new push, so a commit can reach Ready with no Wait and no proof entry.
why: The `head-differs` row says "push and mark again" and the `run-review` route says "then mark again", so the agent marks right after a push: on GitLab that can read the older green pipeline, which is the case D-54 says Wait narrows, and the commit also never reaches `proofs`, as line 68 requires, because `open` does not run again.
fix: State once in Ship that any push after step 1 returns to step 1, and point the `head-differs`, `ci-red` and `run-review` routes at it.
evidence: Added line 65: "2. **Wait.** Run `watch` with `id` as a background shell"; added line 68: "list each such commit in `proofs`"; added line 70: "run that subtask's review to its stop, then mark again"; context line 71, not updated: "push and mark again, or run from the branch of the change". D-54: "on GitLab, a mark just after a push can read the green result of an older commit. The \"Wait\" step of the skill narrows this". `mark_ready_if_green` reads no proof, so nothing else catches the skip. Unverified: GitLab `head_pipeline` behaviour is taken from D-54, which says it was not tested live; `gitlab.py:52` does read `head_pipeline`.

finding: `next: developer` tells the agent "this review has stopped and cannot clear" for failures that are not stopped reviews, and it contradicts the new `command-failed` row.
why: `_why_open` sends every code outside REVIEW_CAN_RUN to `developer`, so a timeout or crash of `finish` (which a retry can clear), a `bad-state`, an empty plan folder or a missing report all read as a stopped review, and a crashed review never reaches the row at line 81 that says to run the command once more.
fix: Route `command-failed` from the review to `mark-again`, and reword `next: developer` to cover every case that reaches it.
evidence: SKILL.md line 70: "`next: developer`: this review has stopped and cannot clear: report `why`"; line 81: "`command-failed` | the forge or review command crashed or ran past its limit | run the command once more"; ci_watch.py line 284: `"run-review" if error.get("code") in REVIEW_CAN_RUN else "developer"`; ci_watch.py line 300: `"next": "developer"` for a plan folder with no contract.

finding: The review's change is matched against the id and the number only, so a review begun with the change url refuses a mark given by number.
why: Failing input: code-review `begin` with change="https://github.com/a/b/pull/7", then `mark-ready` with id="7": the set is {"7"}, the url is not in it, and the gate answers `next: developer` although the review is on this change. The review cannot move to the number form, because `begin` refuses `change-mismatch` and `finish` has stopped it. The new test covers only the other direction (id is the url, review holds the number).
fix: Add the view's url to the set: {change, str(view.get("id")), view.get("url")}, and add a test with the url in the review state and the number in `id`.
evidence: `open_reviews = _open_reviews(plan, {change, str(view.get("id"))})`; `if str(answer.get("change")) not in change_ids:`. code-review SKILL.md Input: "change id | the invocation", which sets no form. The "same form" line in create-change-request SKILL.md binds only that skill's commands. Read from code; not run.

finding: A review command that crashed or ran past its limit gets `next: developer`, which the skill reads as a review that has stopped and cannot clear.
why: Failing input: `finish` passes REVIEW_LIMIT (900 s) while it posts: `_call` answers `command-failed`, not in REVIEW_CAN_RUN, so the entry is `next: developer`. `_post` saves after each comment, so another mark can finish the work, but the agent is told to report and stop. The skill's `command-failed` row says to run the command once more, but a review failure never reaches that row, because it is wrapped in `review-open`. `bad-state` and `internal` get the same false meaning.
fix: Route `command-failed` to `next: mark-again`, and change the `next: developer` text so it also covers a review that cannot be read, not only a stopped one.
evidence: `"run-review" if error.get("code") in REVIEW_CAN_RUN else "developer"`. SKILL.md:70 "`next: developer`: this review has stopped and cannot clear". SKILL.md:81 "`command-failed` | the forge or review command crashed or ran past its limit | run the command once more". Test param: `{"code": "command-failed", ...}, "no answer", "developer"`.

finding: The new gate order puts all `finish` calls between the head check and `change-ready`, and the head and the draft flag are not read again.
why: Failing input: a plan with many subtasks, where each `finish` can take up to 900 s, and a person or another session pushes during those calls. The head check passed on the old commit, `ci-status` then reads the new commit, and the change goes Ready on a head that was never compared with the local head. `marked` also rests on the old `view.draft`. Before this delta, the head check was next to the CI read, so the window was short. D-52 keeps CI last for freshness but does not give the head the same guarantee.
fix: After `_open_reviews`, read `change-view` again and repeat the state and head checks just before the CI read; use that second view for the `draft` check.
evidence: `view = forge_answer("change-view", payload, id=change)` ... `if not local or local != view.get("head_sha"):` ... `open_reviews = _open_reviews(plan, {change, str(view.get("id"))})` ... `ci = forge_answer("ci-status", payload, id=change)`; `REVIEW_LIMIT = 900`. D-52: "The CI read stays last, because it must be the freshest read before `change-ready`". Read from code; not run.

finding: The new `_with_retries` branch has no test: neither the retry after a PermissionError nor the end of its tries.
why: Removing the retry or changing what happens after 20 tries fails no test, and the end of the tries has effects no test pins: `_read_record` gives `bad-record`, `_is_current` reads that as not current so the watch reports `superseded`, and `_write_record` raises out of the watch.
fix: Add tests that patch the read and `os.replace` to raise PermissionError: once (the call succeeds) and on every try (the answer is pinned).
evidence: `def _with_retries(action):` with `except PermissionError: time.sleep(FILE_PAUSE)`. A search of afkv2/tests/skills/test_change_request.py for `_with_retries`, `FILE_TRIES` and `PermissionError` finds 0 lines. The real-process test reaches it only when the Windows race happens. Found by reading; no test was run.

finding: The `run-review` route is proved only on hand-written error codes, never on an answer of the real review command.
why: The 4 rows repeat the words in `REVIEW_CAN_RUN`, so if a code in review_rounds.py is renamed these rows still pass while the gate sends a review that can run to `developer` and stops the run for no reason.

The new real-command tests cover `developer` (twice) and `mark-again`. Line 806 asserts only `subtask` and line 808 only `code`. Codes read at review_rounds.py lines 83, 132, 317, 352.

finding: No test pins the gate's answer for `stopped_by: cap` with a round-3 fix that no round read.
why: `finish` reports that case with `left.blocking` empty and `reviewed: false`, `_why_open` reads neither field and returns None, so the change can go Ready, and this edge of "settled" (D-46) can change with no test failing.
fix: Add a row or a real-command case with `stopped_by: cap`, `left.blocking: []`, `fixed: [{reviewed: false}]`, and assert the answer that the decision wants.
evidence: `({**SETTLED, "stopped_by": "unfixed", "left": {"blocking": [{"id": "f1"}], ...` is the only row with another `stopped_by`; a search for `"cap"` in the test file finds 0 lines. test_code_review.py test_a_fix_in_the_last_round_is_reported_as_not_reviewed shows the report shape. D-46 allows this result, so this is a missing pin, not a proved wrong answer.

finding: Possible misuse: `mark-ready` accepts `forge` and `repo` but honours them for only part of its calls.
why: With a `repo` other than `origin`, the view, CI and Ready calls go to that repo, while `finish` posts findings by bare change number on the origin repo: a wrong change with the same number, or a `not_posted` entry that routes `mark-again` with no way to clear; the `_why_open` guard compares only the id.
fix: Refuse `repo` and `forge` on `mark-ready` when they differ from what the repository resolves to, or carry them through the review state and `finish` in a change coordinated with the code-review owner.
evidence: SKILL.md:20 "The posts that `mark-ready` causes through the review find the forge from the repository." ci_watch.py:55 `_call(REVIEW, "finish", {"plan": str(plan), "subtask": subtask}, REVIEW_LIMIT)`. review_rounds.py:230 `payload = {"id": state["change"], "text": _comment_text(entry)}` holds no forge or repo. ci_watch.py:288 `if str(answer.get("change")) not in change_ids`. Read from the code; the cross-repo path was not run.

RATIONALE.md, "Moved to the change": "Ticket provenance", "Change-specific choices". Unverified: whether RATIONALE.md counts a docstring as a comment under its "Required API documentation" exception; `afkv2/tests/ports/test_tracker_read_back.py:1` has the same form (decision D-33).

finding: `previous.state` can now hold the refusal code `bad-record` under `ok: true`, and the skill's `state` table has no such word.

finding: A small `interval`, which the skill now documents, makes a slice of the watch pass its process limit, and the watch ends `no-verdict` while CI still runs.
why: Failing input: `start` with interval=1 and the default budget. `common.ci_wait` counts only sleep time in `elapsed`, so a 600 s slice is 600 s of sleep plus about 600 reads of `gh pr view`. At about 1 s per read that is about 1200 s, which is more than the limit `wait + READ_MARGIN` (900 s). `_call` kills the command and answers `command-failed`. The default interval of 180 s is safe.
fix: Refuse an `interval` below a floor (for example 30 s) in `_seconds`, or state the floor in the skill line.
evidence: SKILL.md:44 "`interval` is the seconds between its reads"; ci_watch.py:254 `call_forge("ci-wait", {...}, wait + READ_MARGIN)`; ports/forge/common.py:128-130 `wait = min(interval, budget - elapsed)`, `elapsed += wait`. The time per read is an estimate, not measured.

finding: `_last_result` catches only Refusal, so a record with a `beat_at` that is not a number still stops `start`.
why: Failing input: a record file holding {"token":"a","state":"watching","beat_at":null}. `_read_record` accepts it, `_report` raises TypeError at `time.time() - record.get("beat_at", 0)`, and `serve` answers `internal` with no new watch. `status` fails in the same way, so the fix that the `bad-record` text names cannot run. The docstring says a broken record cannot stop the new watch. The new test params do not cover this shape.
fix: Check in `_read_record` that `beat_at` is a number, and refuse `bad-record` when it is not.
evidence: `"""What the last watch found. A broken record is a result here, so that it cannot stop the new watch."""`; `if not isinstance(record, dict) or "token" not in record or "state" not in record:`; test param `["{broken", '{"token": "a"}', "[]"]`. Read from code; not run. Atomic writes make this shape rare: only an outside edit can produce it (inferred).

finding: `fetched: true` is not proof of fresh facts in a clone whose refspec does not track the target.
why: Failing input: a clone made with `--single-branch` of the feature branch. `git fetch origin main` exits 0 and updates only FETCH_HEAD. `_resolved_target` then uses an old `origin/main` or local `main`, or refuses `no-target`, and the answer says `fetched: true`. The skill tells the agent to flag stale facts only on `fetched: false`, so the mergeability case rests on stale facts with no message.
fix: Fetch with an explicit refspec (`+refs/heads/<name>:refs/remotes/origin/<name>`), so that the fetch always moves `origin/<name>`.
evidence: `return shell.run_tool("git", ["fetch", "--quiet", "origin", name], timeout=FETCH_LIMIT).returncode == 0`; `for candidate in (f"origin/{name}", name):`. Unverified: based on git's documented fetch behavior. A probe in the scratch folder was refused by the session's guard, so it was not run.

finding: `"/" not in path.name` cannot fail, because a pathlib name never holds a separator.
why: This half of the assert passes with or without the file-name clean-up, so it reads as proof but gives none; the parent-folder assert on line 573 is what catches an unclean URL.
fix: Remove that half, and assert the file name itself, or write and read a record through a URL id.
evidence: `assert "/" not in path.name and ":" not in path.name`

finding: The test named "a longer limit" takes its expected value from the production constants, so it does not prove the limit is longer.
why: With `READ_MARGIN = 0` this test and the short-budget test still pass, yet the port also reads once more when the budget ends, so the process limit would then end each slice as `command-failed` and the watch as `no-verdict`.
fix: Assert `limit > sent["budget"]` with a literal least margin, and assert `LOST_AFTER > SLICE + READ_MARGIN` so that a normal read cannot read as lost.
evidence: `assert reads == [(ci_watch.SLICE, ci_watch.SLICE + ci_watch.READ_MARGIN)] * 2`. afkv2/ports/forge/CONTRACT.md `ci-wait`: "It reads at least once, and once more when the budget ends." Found by reading; no test was run.

finding: The broken-record cases leave out a record with a `beat_at` that is not a number, and that record still stops `start`.
why: `_last_result` says a broken record cannot stop the new watch, but `_read_record` accepts `{"token": "a", "state": "watching", "beat_at": null}`, `_report` raises TypeError on `time.time() - None`, and `_last_result` catches only Refusal, so `start` answers `internal` and starts no watch.
fix: Add that record to the parameter list, and make `_read_record` or `_report` treat it as `bad-record`.
evidence: `@pytest.mark.parametrize("broken", ["{broken", '{"token": "a"}', "[]"])`; ci_watch.py line 159 `time.time() - record.get("beat_at", 0) > LOST_AFTER`; line 183 `except Refusal as refusal:`. Found by reading; not run.

finding: Possible misuse: the watch record is keyed on the raw `id` text, and the sentence in the skill is the only guard against a split record.
why: `start` with a url and `status` with the number read 2 records, so `status` answers `none` while a watch runs and routes the agent to `start`; `mark-ready` already accepts both forms, so the 2 forms are an expected input.
fix: Derive the record key from the change number, for example the trailing number of a url, so that both forms name one record, and remove the sentence.
evidence: SKILL.md:15 "Give the same form in each command: a url and a number read as 2 watches". ci_watch.py:115 `file_name = _NOT_A_FILE_NAME.sub("_", change)`. ci_watch.py:317 `{change, str(view.get("id"))}`. test_change_request.py `test_a_change_given_as_a_url_matches_the_review_of_its_number`.

finding: The `target-differs` refusal carries the change's target only in the `reason` prose, while its next action needs that value.
why: The skill routes this refusal to "read the merge facts for the target of the change", so the agent must parse a sentence to get the input of its next call; the sibling refusals `not-draft` and `ci-*` carry their values as fields.
fix: Add the value as a field: `Refusal("target-differs", ..., target=view["target"])`, and name the field in the SKILL.md row.
evidence: change_request.py:125 `raise Refusal("target-differs", f"change {view['id']} targets {view['target']}, not {payload['target']}")`. SKILL.md:77 "read the merge facts for the target of the change". change_request.py:118 `raise Refusal("not-draft", ..., id=created["id"], url=view.get("url"))`.

finding: The new field list of `merge-facts` omits `target`, does not say `ahead` and `behind` can be null, and misdescribes `fetched: false` for a local-only target.
why: The answer holds the resolved `target`, which shows whether the facts rest on `origin/<name>` or on a local branch; a target that only this clone holds gives `fetched: false`, and the skill reads that as "the last fetch", though no fetch ever read that branch.
fix: List `target` in the answer, state that `ahead` and `behind` are null when git gives no count, and say that `fetched: false` with a `target` that has no `origin/` prefix means a local branch.
evidence: SKILL.md:27 "answers `clean`, `conflicts`, `ahead`, `behind` and `fetched`"; "`fetched: false` means the facts rest on the last fetch". change_request.py:168 `return ok(target=target, fetched=fetched, clean=..., conflicts=conflicts,`. change_request.py:148 `return int(done.stdout.strip()) if done.returncode == 0 else None`. test_change_request.py `test_merge_facts_read_a_target_that_only_this_clone_holds`.
